title: South Korea's Demographic Crisis
author: Staff Writer
description: South Korean authorities launched a flurry of initiatives in 2025 aimed at reversing the country's demographic collapse—part of a broader effort to nudge up the world's lowest fertility rate. Population figures have now declined for four consecutive years, and the country's GDP per capita recently slipped to fifth in Asia, behind Taiwan, whose fertility rate is only marginally higher. Despite earlier optimism following announcements of state support, 190,000 babies were born, marking a 6.9 percent year-over-year increase—the largest since 2007. Much of this uptick has been driven by women in their early 30s—those born in the mid-1990s, during one of South Korea's strongest economic periods.
